prompts.task: Use $otel-instrument for a focused, read-only logging repair plan for ./service. Read the real baseline app.py and manifest separately from eval/inputs/logging-contract-evidence.json. The evidence is a synthetic candidate overlay with supplied observations, not live execution or actual baseline instrumentation. Assess every observation and control case against OpenTelemetry logging guidance and the stated operator policy. Identify concrete faults with evidence and the smallest safe language-specific repair and acceptance test; distinguish SDK-owned defaults, unsupported/unverified capability, legitimate opt-ins and optional absent fields from missing application wiring. Save supplemental .observe/logging-instrument.json and .observe/logging-instrument.md with per-observation and per-control decisions, reasoning, source citations, and exact future tests. For this explicitly plan-only evaluation do not produce or alter canonical audit/selection/instrumentation reports, edit source/dependencies/config/tests, install packages, execute applications/probes, use network/cloud/models/browser, or claim any runtime/receipt test passed. Do not widen scope to the baseline service general instrumentation gaps. Keep actual runtime verification Not run/Not proven. Keep both reports concise: at most 1600 words combined, with a compact decision for each observation/control and shared acceptance details.

judge_inputs: Inspect service/.observe/logging-instrument.json and .md, original source and eval/inputs/logging-contract-evidence.json; inspect trace.jsonl, grade.json and last_message.md. This is explicitly plan-only; never demand an executed runtime or canonical reports. Control cases prevent treating optional or SDK-owned behavior as missing.
rubric: Keeps baseline source facts separate from synthetic overlay observations, writes only supplemental requested reports, covers every observation and control case, cites concrete evidence, and makes no installation/runtime/delivery success claims. Uses the loaded skill and its applicable guidance; current installed capability remains unverified.

Finds the event timestamp overwritten by observed/export time and incorrect numeric ERROR=8; proposes retaining occurrence precision and source severity via the detected official bridge, ERROR in 17-20 range, unknown optional severity not fabricated. For Node explicitly avoids Number precision loss for nanosecond timestamps. Does not require equality of event and observation times.

Identifies missing unsampled log under default trace_based=false and stale IDs after detach; proposes exact in-span sampled/unsampled IDs and flags plus no-context and concurrent/async isolation tests. Preserves explicitly supported operator trace_based=true drops in the explicit-filter control; does not force sampling or fabricate spans to satisfy correlation.

Finds privacy exposure in body, stack and error.dump, replaces invented exception mapping with allowed exception.type where applicable, and omits disallowed message/stack. Applies privacy before export including nested/formatter paths. Does not force EventName or instrumentation-specific exception-event migration/severity onto the existing bridge; ordinary messages and bridge-exception controls are valid without EventName.

Finds mismatch with selected body/attribute policy; explains span limits do not bound log attributes and log attribute value limits do not bound Body. Plans supported log-specific limits or public API with separate body policy, oversized boundary tests, and accounting where supported. Treats sdk-owned control as covered by defaults/tests rather than demanding application overrides, arbitrary new limits or an additional provider.

Finds unbounded log queue, span-only BSP settings, unbounded shutdown, and false complete claim despite two partial-success rejections. Plans bounded log batching/settings via supported BLRP or public APIs, batch<=queue, fault/overload and final-log shutdown tests. Counts 3 attempted, 1 accepted, 2 rejected separately; does not claim durable/exactly-once delivery or infer receipt from enqueue/HTTP200/flush.

Finds recursive exporter diagnostics and halted app progress; proposes separate diagnostic routing or SDK suppression and an outage test proving bounded diagnostics/export attempts, continued application/original sink and unaffected configured signals. Keeps the existing language-specific provider/bridge owner and local-only destination, rather than adding a duplicate SDK/bridge or sending logs to cloud.
